Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

dē

dē (+ ablative)

preposition with the ablative

from, down from; off, down from

In this lexicon

  • from

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 12.2.2: dē viā rēctā ad mē

  • off

    the recommended word · classical · Vulg. Mt. 15.27: mīcīs quae cadunt dē mēnsā; Plaut. Cas. 931: dēcidō dē lectō praecipes

  • dē + abl.: about

    classical

  • relātiō dē mendō: bug report

    our formation

  • dē mendō referre: bug report

    our formation

  • relātiō dē vitiō: bug report

    our formation

  • labōrāre dē (+ ablative): concern

    classical

  • dē autoraedā ēgredī: get out

    modern

  • dē pretiō pacīscī: haggle

    classical

  • dē + abl.: of

    classical

  • dē rē pūblicā: political

    classical

  • dē imprōvīsō (ex imprōvīsō): suddenly

    classical

  • dē imprōvīsō opprimō, opprimere, oppressī, oppressum: surprise

    classical

Examples

  • jam tē vidēbō et quidem, ut spērō, dē viā rēctā ad mē

    I shall see you soon, and, I hope, straight from the road to my houseCic. Att. 12.2.2

    In the entry for from

  • nam et catellī edunt dē mīcīs quae cadunt dē mēnsā dominōrum suōrum

    for even the little dogs eat of the crumbs that fall off their masters’ tableVulg. Mt. 15.27

    In the entry for off

  • dēcidō dē lectō praecipes: subsilit, optundit ōs mihi

    I tumble headlong off the couch; he jumps on me and punches me in the facePlaut. Cas. 931

    In the entry for off

  • dē digitō ānulum dētrahō

    I take the ring off my fingerTer. Heaut. 650–651

    In the entry for off

  • tam ineptum erit quam flēre quod arboribus amoenīs et domum tuam ōrnantibus dēcidant folia

    it will be as silly as weeping because the leaves fall off the lovely trees that adorn your houseSen. Ep. 104.11

    In the entry for off
